significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that a partially truth-orthogonal “provenance direction” distinguishes parametric from contextual beliefs, that its “collapse” produces source-attribution errors, and that steering it can correct attribution “without changing the encoded truth-value”; this is principally a form-(ii) causal mechanism of the separable-direction-plus-repair shape, not a transferable law. It establishes both a phenomenon—source misattribution under memory–context conflict—and a mechanism separating provenance from truth, thereby constraining whether such errors should be explained as failed source tagging rather than failed truth representation, but it does not fix expectations for unrelated belief failures. The negative branch would meaningfully rule out this separable provenance-tag account, and true versus false are determinate despite “belief-vs-fact errors” being less precisely specified than source-attribution errors. Topic substitution removes the distinctive truth-preserving provenance intervention and leaves only generic research on belief representations, which would not earn this score; the claim is somewhat sharper than the topic-median direction-and-steering hypothesis but remains bounded by one closely related error class.

reach.justification: The transferable handles named in the claim are the “provenance index,” “source-misattribution-rate,” and causally steerable “provenance direction”; the index can be an ex-ante warning if activation collapse predicts an attribution error before the answer is emitted, whereas the misattribution rate itself is post hoc. After recalibration on another model, however, the conclusion supplies mainly a procedure for recovering a new direction rather than a quantitative relation predicting that model’s geometry or error rate. The hypothesis speaks broadly of “an LLM” and could support auditing or gating systems that must distinguish retrieved context from parametric memory, but it explicitly allows effects to “vary across model families and scale,” and no cross-family invariant or practitioner-ready threshold is asserted. Under topic substitution these concrete provenance handles disappear, so the score is attributable to the claim rather than to the general importance of LLM-belief research; its ex-ante diagnostic potential raises it slightly above the default post-hoc probe-and-steering deliverable.
